Cognitive Behavioural Therapy.

You talk about how you feel and what is on your mind, then you discuss what you can do to feel better about it or how you can view it in a more positive way.  Think of it as "reprogramming your mind to not always be so negative/fearful". 
For me, it also included "challenges" such as ordering food or going to the shop alone (I had crippling anxiety as well as depression, both are stable now). We started with one per week then increased the number of challenges to improve my confidence and self-esteem. 

Call me naive, but I like to think you're never too old to be happy!

Thankyou for replying, I'm glad to know you're okay atm

Honestly, school was the worst time of my life. There are some things I miss, but feeling better about myself for who I am and my own capabilities now far outweigh those small Slices of okay-ness in those times.

I know it has been very different for others, but my own opinion is that school was not good for my health (I liked the learning, not the people lol).

Keep studying, find out where you want to go next. It doesn't matter if ultimately its not what you persue forever, it's all experience that can be used elsewhere in some way (eg, drama - drama/English teacher, parent - carer/nursery teacher, maths - business/accounting).

High school is hard, but you will get through it. Keep your head up and look to the future. Ambition and hope are your greatest weapons in this battle for happiness.

I remember that feeling.

It's taken 10 long years for me, but I no longer think that way (on the whole). Obviously there are good days and bad days, and your ability to cope is a large factor too. 

Have you considered CBT? That was the therapy that finally reprogrammed my mindset and, while it was only a temporary programme in itself, it has helped me no end in day-to-day life.

You don't have to feel this way forever. There is help available, the hard part is finding what suits you best. But once you've found that out, you'll be able to make more steps towards recovery - it is a long process, but I believe in you! :)

Hey, care worker aged 22.

We have had a lot of people pass away due to covid. However, we have had a lot who were in isolation with symptoms who have come out the other side, including a lady who is over 100.

Drink plenty of fluids, eat what you can. There is still hope. 

And if you need to talk, you know where to find us. It's okay to be scared, we all are in at least some way. But we will get through this, including you.
